title: A training load you actually keep
outcomes: Separates a planned load from a recorded one and works out what share of a plan was kept
Sets a weekly load from the last two weeks of his own record
Sorts a load set from the record, an unkept plan, a restart at the old load and a short holiday
Writes a staged re-entry plan for a break of two weeks or more

steps.text: A **training load** is the chess work you do in a week: sessions and minutes. The number that counts is the one you *did*, not the one you planned. More hours alone do not promise progress, because players differ a lot in how long improvement takes. This app promises no number of hours and no rating. The aim is a load you can keep, checked against your record.

steps.prompt: Work these out before you read on. (1) You planned 10 hours (600 minutes) and your record shows 3 hours (180 minutes). (2) Two weeks of record: 270 minutes, then 180 minutes.

fields.label: Percent of the plan you kept:
Average minutes per week over the two weeks:

steps.text: **Set the load from the record.** Look at the last two weeks, not at your hopes. A rule of thumb to test: start at or just below your *lower* week, and raise the load only after a week in which you did everything you planned. With 270 and 180 minutes, a first load of 180 is a sensible guess. It is a guess, not a proven rule.

steps.prompt: Sort each case. Does setting the load from the record work, fail, or not apply? Choose, then save to see my answer. The answers are my judgement, not a measurement.

fields.label: Plan: 10 hours a week. Record for two weeks: 3 hours and 3 hours. Next week's plan: 10 hours again.
Record: 3 hours and 3 hours. Plan: 3 hours, compared with the record every Sunday.
After a break of two weeks you restart at the old load of 8 hours.
A holiday of two days in an otherwise normal week.

steps.text: **After a break.** After a gap of about two weeks or more, restore the load in stages instead of jumping back. One plan to try: half of the old load in week 1, three quarters in week 2, the full load in week 3, if the earlier weeks were kept. The fractions are a guess to adjust. A day or two off needs no plan.

steps.prompt: Your old load was 240 minutes a week. Use the staged plan above.

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** The app sees only what you do inside it, does not total your minutes and sends no reminders. The weekly record is yours, on paper or in a note. *My plan* compares silent exercise scores before and after a period; write your load in its "What will you do" box. Then set the next load yourself.
